title: Limit of a Function and Limit Laws
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Informal Definition of a Limit
definitions.statement: If f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to a single number L as x approaches c from both sides (without ever requiring x = c), we say that the limit of f(x) as x approaches c is L.
conditions: f must be defined in an open interval containing c, except possibly at c itself
L must be a unique, finite real number
definitions.explanation: The value of f at x = c is completely irrelevant to the existence or value of the limit. The limit describes local behavior near c, not at c.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Limits describe the target value of f(x) near c, independent of f(c).

definitions.title: Algebraic Limit Laws
definitions.latex: \lim_{x \to c} [f(x) \pm g(x)] = L \pm M, \quad \lim_{x \to c} [f(x)g(x)] = LM, \quad \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \frac{L}{M} \quad (M \neq 0)
definitions.statement: If lim_{x->c} f(x) = L and lim_{x->c} g(x) = M exist, then limits distribute linearly across sums, differences, constant multiples, products, quotients (with non-zero denominator), powers, and roots.
conditions: Both individual limits must exist as finite numbers
In quotient law, the limit of the denominator M must be non-zero
definitions.explanation: These laws allow evaluation of complicated expressions term-by-term without recurring to epsilon-delta proofs.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Limits distribute over standard algebraic operations provided each individual limit exists.

definitions.title: The Sandwich (Squeeze) Theorem
definitions.latex: g(x) \le f(x) \le h(x) \implies \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \quad \text{when } \lim_{x \to c} g(x) = \lim_{x \to c} h(x) = L
definitions.statement: If g(x) <= f(x) <= h(x) for all x in an open interval containing c (except possibly c), and lim_{x->c} g(x) = lim_{x->c} h(x) = L, then lim_{x->c} f(x) = L.
conditions: Inequality holds in a punctured neighborhood of c
Both bounding functions converge to the exact same limit L
definitions.explanation: Essential for evaluating oscillatory limits such as x^2 * sin(1/x) near 0 where direct substitution fails.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Trap an unknown function between two known bounds that converge to the same limit.

definitions.title: Cancellation Rule for 0/0 Forms
definitions.statement: If direct substitution into a rational function yields 0/0, (x - c) is a common factor of both numerator and denominator. Factoring and canceling (x - c) produces an identical function near c.
conditions: Cancellation is valid because x approaches c but never equals c
definitions.explanation: By the Factor Theorem, c being a zero implies (x - c) divides the polynomial.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Always factor and cancel common linear factors (x - c) when encountering 0/0 in rational functions.
